passages.scripture: This is a trustworthy saying: If anyone aspires to be an overseer, he desires a noble task.

lines.text: A church is God’s people — everyone who belongs to Jesus, gathered together.
An overseer is a leader who watches over and cares for a church.
Being an overseer is a noble task — good and honorable work.
To aspire to be an overseer is to reach for that work and long for it.
Here is a saying: “If anyone aspires to be an overseer, he desires a noble task.”
Paul says this saying is trustworthy — people can rely on this saying.

passages.scripture: An overseer, then, must be above reproach, the husband of but one wife, temperate, self-controlled, respectable, hospitable, able to teach, not dependent on wine, not violent but gentle, peaceable, and free of the love of money.

lines.text: Being an overseer is a noble task, so an overseer must live in a way that fits that task.
An overseer must be above reproach — no one can rightly accuse him of doing wrong.
An overseer must be the husband of only one wife.
An overseer must be temperate — sober and clear-minded.
An overseer must be self-controlled — able to rule his own thoughts and desires.
An overseer must be respectable — living in an orderly way that others can respect.
An overseer must be hospitable — glad to welcome guests and strangers into his home.
An overseer must be able to teach — able to explain God’s word to others.
An overseer must not be dependent on wine — he must not be a drunkard.
An overseer must not be violent — he must not hit people or pick fights.
Instead, an overseer must be gentle — kind and patient with people.
An overseer must be peaceable — not quarrelsome.
An overseer must be free of the love of money — not greedy for money.

passages.scripture: An overseer must manage his own household well and keep his children under control, with complete dignity.

lines.text: An overseer must manage his own household well — he must lead and care for his family and everyone in his home.
An overseer must keep his children under control — his children must obey him.
An overseer’s home must have complete dignity — a reverent, serious, worthy way of living that earns respect.

passages.scripture: For if someone does not know how to manage his own household, how can he care for the church of God?

lines.text: If a man does not know how to manage his own household, how can he take care of the church of God?
A man who cannot lead his own family well is not ready to take care of God’s people.

passages.scripture: He must not be a recent convert, or he may become conceited and fall under the same condemnation as the devil.

lines.text: A recent convert is someone who has only just come to believe in Jesus — like a plant newly put into the ground.
An overseer must not be a recent convert.
To be conceited is to be puffed up with pride — to think too highly of yourself.
A recent convert who is made a leader too soon may become conceited.
The devil, also called Satan, is an enemy of God and of God’s people.
Condemnation is being judged guilty and sentenced to punishment.
The devil was prideful and fell under condemnation himself.
The devil is also called the accuser of God’s people, because he accuses them before God.
A conceited overseer may fall under the same condemnation as the devil.

passages.scripture: Furthermore, he must have a good reputation with outsiders, so that he will not fall into disgrace and into the snare of the devil.

lines.text: A good reputation means people speak well of you because of how you live.
Outsiders are people who do not belong to the church.
An overseer must also have a good reputation with outsiders.
Disgrace is being spoken against and looked down on by others.
Then the overseer will not fall into disgrace.
A snare is a trap, like one used to catch a bird or an animal.
Then the overseer will not fall into the snare of the devil.
